question: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 11 and 330, respectively. If one of the numbers is 110, find the other one.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know that the product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

Second Number = (11 × 330) ÷ 110

Second Number = 11 × 3 = 33

**∴ The correct answer is 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF = 11

LCM = 330

First Number = 110

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = HCF × LCM

**Calculations:**

⇒ 110 × Second Number = 11 × 330

⇒ 110 × Second Number = 3630

⇒ Second Number = 3630 ÷ 110

⇒ Second Number = 33

**∴ The correct answer is 33.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule for Two Numbers

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of the numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b). Note that this rule strictly applies only to two numbers, not three or more.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their highest common factor (HCF) is 1. For such numbers, their least common multiple (LCM) is directly the product of the two numbers.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators)
LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)
